body:
## Bug

https://qelectrotech.org/bugtracker/view.php?id=291

Clicking Cancel on the "Open Element" dialog (Element Editor > Ctrl+O) before the collection tree finishes loading crashes the application with an "unhandled pointer exception."

## Root cause

`ElementsCollectionModel::loadCollections()` (`sources/ElementsCollection/elementscollectionmodel.cpp`) kicks off `QtConcurrent::map(m_items_list_to_setUp, setUpData)`, running `setUpData()` on each `ElementCollectionItem*` from the model's own item tree on worker threads — but nothing ever cancels or waits for that `QFuture`. The model had no destructor at all.

`ElementDialog::getOpenElementLocation()` (used by the Element Editor's "Open" action) constructs one of these models to populate its tree, then deletes the whole dialog on Cancel. Deleting the dialog destroys the model, and `QStandardItemModel`'s destructor deletes all its `QStandardItem`/`ElementCollectionItem` rows. If the background `QtConcurrent::map()` pass is still running at that moment — i.e. the user cancels *before* loading finishes — worker threads keep calling `setUpData()` on those now-freed items concurrently with their destruction: a textbook use-after-free. This matches the report precisely: canceling *after* loading completes is safe (no worker threads left to race), while canceling fast is not.

## Fix

Add a destructor to `ElementsCollectionModel` that calls `m_future.cancel()` (stops any not-yet-started work items) then `m_future.waitForFinished()` (blocks until any in-flight `setUpData()` calls actually complete), before `QStandardItemModel`'s own destructor starts tearing down the item tree.

## Verification

- Clean rebuild: only the intended files recompiled, linked successfully.
- I built both a pre-fix and post-fix binary and attempted a live repro under Xvfb — opening the Element Editor, pressing Ctrl+O then Escape immediately, repeated ~40 times in rapid succession — but could not trigger the crash on either binary. The test collection in this sandbox is small with a warm disk cache, so `loadCollections()` likely completes faster than synthetic `xdotool` keypresses can race it, unlike the reporter's presumably larger/colder real-world collection.
- Confidence in the fix rests on the use-after-free being unambiguous from the code itself (worker threads hold no lifetime guard on items whose owning model can be deleted out from under them), and the fix directly closes that window before destruction proceeds. No regression observed in either binary's normal open/cancel behavior.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
